newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Seen weak, but held up by swaps.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Seen weak, but held up by swaps.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices ignored bearish residue stock figures to firm by a dollar from Wednesday, tracking healthy swaps quotes, traders said on Thursday.
Residues stocks in Singapore were up by 820,000 barrels at 10.914 million barrels, according to the latest figures from the Trade Development Board.

But cash prices in the Singapore spot market rose marginally from Wednesday. A bid was seen at $99.00 per tonne for February loading supplies against offers at $100.00 per tonne, a dollar higher than Wednesday's quotes.

Traders said cash levels have firmed on healthy sentiment seen in the paper market with players seen buying fuel oil paper and selling Dubai to capture on the wide crack spread pegged at a positive $4.00 per tonne.
The swaps market was active with at least 30,000 tonnes worth of paper volume heard transacted. February swaps were last quoted at $100.00/$101.50 per tonne, up from Wednesday's $99.00/$99.50.
A trader estimated the China had purchased closed to 400,000 tonnes of fuel oil for delivery in February.
"Chinese traders have already closed their books and are not likely to buy anything until after the Lunar New Year," he said.

FOB South Korean and Singapore premiums were still weak, reflecting a market still weighed down by healthy supplies. Traders assessed premiums at par to 50 cents discount FOB South Korea and Singapore.
Regional supplies from South Korea and the Middle East remained on offer.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
